test.name: Extract marriage order and the parental consent signer from an 1893 Hamilton County license
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_029: the record the user pasted is now served as a record_read fixture (the 1893 Hamilton County marriage license entry for Charles Ferber and Emma Schmidt; Jacob Lang, the minor groom's stepfather who signed consent, is carried as a persona. FamilySearch rarely indexes the consent signer, so that shape is deliberate), and extraction runs in code. 1893 Hamilton County, Ohio marriage license and return. The bride is designated a widow on her second marriage, so her recorded surname (Schmidt) is a prior husband's, not her parents'. The underage groom's consent is signed on the reverse by a man whose surname (Lang) differs from his own, i.e. a stepfather or guardian rather than the father. Exercises the marriage-order and consent-signer capture rules; the alpha-team review (2026-08-14) found nothing instructed the extractor to capture either.

judge_context: Override for Correctness and Completeness: the test chooses which record the skill extracts. Do not lower any score because the record concerns people the project objective does not name.

The skill makes one extraction_append call with the record id and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
